title: Tracking changes in body composition: comparison of methods and influence of pre-assessment standardisation (Tinsley et al. 2022)
content: Tinsley GM et al., 2022 — Non-standardised pre-assessment conditions (time of day, fasted vs fed state, hydration, recent exercise) can meaningfully distort the apparent change in body composition between two measurements over time, independent of any real change in tissue. Comparing two readings taken under different conditions risks misattributing normal day-to-day fluctuation to a genuine fat-mass or muscle-mass change.

title: Tracking changes in body composition: comparison of methods and influence of pre-assessment standardisation (Tinsley et al. 2022)
content: Tinsley et al. 2022 — Product implication: confidence in a longitudinal body-composition trend should account for how standardized the measurement conditions were (same time of day, similar fasted/hydration/pre-exercise state across readings) — not treated as uniformly reliable regardless of conditions. Where conditions are known to be inconsistent or unrecorded, trend confidence should be lowered rather than presented at face value.
